en forfader.explanation: "Forfader" is made of "for" (before) and "fader" (an old form of "far", father), so it is literally a "before-father". The plural is irregular: "forfædre", not "forfadere". It is slightly formal; in casual talk Danes might say "mine oldeforældre" (my great-grandparents) for the nearer generations.

sentence.en: My ancestor was a farmer in Jutland.

en fornyelse.explanation: "Fornyelse" is the noun for renewing something, from the verb "at forny" (to renew). It is used for things like passports, contracts and subscriptions, and it can also mean a fresh start or renewal in a more general sense. The prefix "for-" here does not mean "before" but "making it new again", the same pattern as in "forbedring" (improvement).

sentence.da: Det er tid til **fornyelse** af kontrakten.
sentence.en: It is time for renewal of the contract.

at forhandle.explanation: "At forhandle" means to negotiate, for example prices, contracts or pay. You negotiate about something with "om": "forhandle om prisen". Be careful, because the noun "en forhandler" does not mean a negotiator but a dealer or retailer, such as a car dealer.

sentence.en: They are going to negotiate the price.

forms.en: I am telling you this in confidence

fortroligt.explanation: "Fortroligt" is the form of "fortrolig" (confidential, trusted) that you use with et-words, and it is also the word for "confidentially". It is common in work and official settings, for example on documents that are not to be shared.

sentence.da: Jeg siger det **fortroligt**, så sig det ikke til andre.
sentence.en: I'm telling you in confidence, so don't tell anyone else.

femogtredive.explanation: Danish numbers from 21 to 99 put the ones first, then "og" (and), then the tens: fem-og-tredive is literally "five and thirty". It is written as one word. This takes practice, since you have to know the ones before you know the tens, but it follows the same rule all the way to 99.

sentence.en: My brother is thirty-five years old.

forms.da: For pokker, jeg har glemt nøglen!
forms.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

for pokker.explanation: "For pokker" is a mild exclamation like "darn" or "for heaven's sake", used when something annoying or surprising happens. It is harmless and fine to use with anyone, though it sounds a little old-fashioned to younger ears. A similar mild one is "for søren".

sentence.da: **For pokker**, nu har jeg glemt min nøgle!
sentence.en: Darn it, now I've forgotten my key!
